title: Common Differences in k-Term Arithmetic Progressions

problemStatement.formal: For k ≥ 3, define D_k(A) = { d : ∃ a, {a, a+d, ..., a+(k-1)d} ⊆ A }. How does max_{|A|=n} |D_k(A)| grow as a function of n and k? The k=3 case is Erdős #1097 with bounds Ω(n^{1.778}) to O(n^{11/6}). For k ≥ 4 the exponent should decrease.
problemStatement.plain: Generalize the 3-term AP common differences question to k-term APs: how many distinct common differences can k-APs in an n-element set have?
whyMatters: Connects to Szemerédi's theorem and quantitative arithmetic regularity
Anti-monotonicity in k gives a hierarchy of counting problems

proven: D_k is anti-monotone in k: longer arithmetic progressions have no more common differences than shorter ones.
D_k(A) is contained in D_3(A) for k >= 3.
Negation symmetry, subset monotonicity, and an O(n^2) upper bound are formalized.
open: Growth exponent α(4): is it strictly less than α(3)?
